Procedures specific to creating a sending authorization policy are provided for either method. Note Sending authorization policies that you attach to email address identities take precedence over policies that you attach to their corresponding domain identities. For example, if you create a policy for example.com that disallows a delegate sender, and you create a policy for sender@example.com that allows the delegate sender, then the delegate sender can send email from sender@example.com , but not from any other address on the example.com domain. This guide explains how to configure AWS to trust GitHub's OIDC as a federated identity, and includes a workflow example for the aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials that uses tokens to authenticate to AWS and access resources. Prerequisites To learn the basic concepts of how GitHub uses OpenID Connect (OIDC), and its architecture and benefits, see OpenID Connect . To control how your cloud provider issues access tokens, you must define at least one condition, so that untrusted repositories can’t request access tokens for your cloud resources. For more information, see OpenID Connect reference . OIDC tokens requested for Dependabot update jobs have an event_name claim of dynamic . ## 1. Local testing ke liye credentials

Tumhare project `C:\kamlesh\projects\portfolio_api\.env.example` ke according:

| Setting | Local testing |
|---|---|
| `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` | Turso database URL |


```json
  "Statement": [

      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": "ses:SendEmail",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ses:ap-south-1:<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>:identity/<verified-domain-or-email>"
    }
  ]
}
```

Local me preferred approach: separate local SES IAM user/role aur `AWS_PROFILE` use karo. Long-lived keys ko `.env` me dalne se better hai.

## 2. Production Lambda ke liye SES credentials

Lambda environment me ye variables chahiye:

```env

AWS_REGION=ap-south-1
```

- ECR repository me image push
- Existing Lambda function update

```text
└── ECR push
└── Lambda create/update

Lambda execution role
└── CloudWatch logs
└── SES SendEmail only for verified identity

Local SES user/profile
└── SES SendEmail only
```

```text
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
```

```text
GitHub Actions
    ↓ short-lived OIDC token
AWS IAM deployment role
    ↓
ECR push + Lambda update
```

```yaml
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read
```

Aur `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` me deployment role ARN assume hota hai. AWS/GitHub official docs bhi OIDC use karte hain.

- Selected ECR repository me image push
- Selected Lambda function create/update

Sirf IAM permission se email deliver nahi hota:

- `SES_FROM_EMAIL` identity verify honi chahiye.
- Sender aur region same SES region me hone chahiye.
- `ap-south-1` ke andar SES **sandbox** hai.

name: Deploy to AWS Lambda

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  ECR_REPOSITORY: ${{ secrets.ECR_REPOSITORY }}
  LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME: ${{ secrets.LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME }}
  IMAGE_TAG: ${{ github.sha }}

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          aws-region: ap-south-1

      - name: Login to Amazon ECR
        id: ecr-login
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - name: Build & Push image to ECR (arm64)
        id: build-push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/arm64
          push: true
          provenance: false
          sbom: false
          tags: |
            ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }}
            ${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:latest
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      - name: Check if Lambda function exists
        id: check-lambda
        run: |
          if [ -z "$LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME" ]; then
            echo "exists=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "âš ï¸  LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME secret not set â€” skipping Lambda update"
          elif aws lambda get-function --function-name "$LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME" --region ap-south-1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "exists=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "âœ… Lambda function found"
          else
            echo "exists=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "âš ï¸  Lambda function '$LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME' not found â€” skipping update"
          fi

      - name: Update Lambda function code
        if: steps.check-lambda.outputs.exists == 'true'
        run: |
          aws lambda update-function-code \
            --function-name "$LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME" \
            --image-uri "${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }}" \
            --region ap-south-1

          aws lambda wait function-updated \
            --function-name "$LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME" \
            --region ap-south-1

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "### Deploy Summary ðŸš€" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "- Region: \`ap-south-1\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "- Image: \`${{ steps.ecr-login.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.ECR_REPOSITORY }}:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "- Lambda updated: \`${{ steps.check-lambda.outputs.exists }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
